domain_symbols.probabilistic_model: random variables, processes, and statistical models
domain_symbols.uncertainty_structure: uncertainty sets, metrics, and rate descriptions

rules.name: Ito integral isometry seed
rules.input_form: square-integrable adapted Ito integrand
preconditions: The standard Ito integral framework and adaptedness hypotheses hold
rules.operation: Relate the second moment of an Ito integral to a deterministic integral of the integrand square.
examples: Ito isometry converts stochastic integral size control into deterministic integral control
counterexamples: Using nonadapted integrands in the standard Ito-isometry statement is invalid

rules.name: Ito formula seed
rules.input_form: smooth function of an Ito process
preconditions: The process and smoothness assumptions satisfy the standard Ito-formula setting
rules.operation: Apply the stochastic chain rule with quadratic-variation correction.
examples: Stochastic chain rules require second-order correction terms absent from ordinary calculus
counterexamples: Applying the ordinary deterministic chain rule directly to Ito processes is invalid

rules.name: Fisher-Rao metric seed
rules.input_form: regular differentiable statistical model family
preconditions: A regular differentiable parametric model is fixed
rules.operation: Use Fisher information as a local metric tensor on a statistical model family.
examples: Nearby parameter values are compared by local statistical distinguishability encoded through the Fisher metric
counterexamples: Treating arbitrary nondifferentiable model families as automatically Fisher-Rao metric spaces is invalid

rules.name: Uncertainty set seed
rules.input_form: unknown parameter or disturbance class
preconditions: A modeling framework for admissible uncertainty is fixed
rules.operation: Represent uncertainty by sets, distributions, or regions rather than one fixed exact value.
examples: Robust optimization and interval uncertainty use structured admissible sets rather than single exact inputs
counterexamples: Replacing structured uncertainty by one arbitrary guessed parameter value loses the uncertainty model

rules.name: Large-deviation rate seed
rules.input_form: family of rare-event probabilities
preconditions: A standard large-deviation scaling regime is fixed
rules.operation: Describe rare-event decay by an exponential rate function.
examples: Exponentially unlikely events can still be studied structurally through rate-function geometry
counterexamples: Treating every small probability as if it had the same decay mechanism is invalid

rules.name: Stochastic differential equation seed
rules.input_form: drift-diffusion equation with stochastic driver
preconditions: A standard Ito drift-diffusion setting is fixed
rules.operation: Model random evolution through stochastic differential equations.
examples: Random forcing is modeled structurally through differential drift-diffusion form rather than by adding ad hoc noise after a deterministic solve
counterexamples: An arbitrary noisy update rule is not automatically an Ito SDE

rules.name: Martingale representation seed
rules.input_form: adapted martingale in a suitable filtration
preconditions: A filtration and driving-noise model satisfying a representation theorem are fixed
rules.operation: Represent suitable martingales as stochastic integrals against the driving noise.
examples: Stochastic information flow can be encoded through one canonical noise source plus adapted integrands
counterexamples: Representing arbitrary nonadapted processes as martingale integrals is invalid

rules.name: Divergence geometry seed
rules.input_form: statistical model with admissible divergence functional
rules.output_form: local geometric structure from divergence data
preconditions: A smooth statistical model and admissible divergence are fixed
rules.operation: Recover local information geometry from divergence structure.
examples: Relative-entropy-like quantities induce local geometric structure beyond raw parameter distance
counterexamples: Treating arbitrary dissimilarity scores as information-geometric divergences without structural conditions is invalid

rules.name: Distributionally robust uncertainty seed
rules.input_form: ambiguity set of admissible probability laws
preconditions: An ambiguity-set construction and decision objective are fixed
rules.operation: Model uncertainty through admissible families of distributions rather than one single law.
examples: Optimization or inference can remain valid across whole neighborhoods of distributions rather than one estimated law only
counterexamples: Replacing ambiguity classes by one guessed nominal distribution loses distributional robustness

rules.name: Concentration inequality seed
rules.input_form: random quantity with admissible tail or dependence assumptions
preconditions: Independence, boundedness, tail, or martingale assumptions are fixed
rules.operation: Bound deviation probabilities without computing the full distribution exactly.
examples: Rare large fluctuations can be controlled without computing the full distribution exactly
counterexamples: Applying concentration results with no independence, boundedness, or tail hypotheses is invalid

rules.name: Rare-event sampling seed
rules.input_form: rare-event probability estimator with changed sampling law
preconditions: A valid importance-sampling change of measure and weight correction are fixed
rules.operation: Estimate tiny probabilities efficiently by weighted rare-event sampling.
examples: Sampling from a tilted distribution can estimate tiny probabilities far more effectively than naive Monte Carlo
counterexamples: Changing the sampling law without correcting weights is invalid

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion
rules.input_form: raw expression E
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Rewrite expressions into a canonical form that preserves the active equivalence relation.
examples: x + y and y + x map to a shared canonical additive form in commutative settings
counterexamples: Applying canonicalization rules outside their preconditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Substitution soundness expansion
rules.input_form: expression F(x) with admissible substitution x <- g
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Substitute only under explicit domain and structural admissibility constraints.
examples: Replacing a variable by a constrained expression must preserve declared domain assumptions
counterexamples: Substitution that violates assumptions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Composition rule expansion

rules.operation: Compose structured objects when composition preconditions are satisfied.
